title: Finite-surjective Zariski refinement of an etale covering
statement: Let $S$ be a reduced Noetherian scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Let $(u_i:U_i\to S)_{i\in I}$ be a jointly surjective family [def-weil-surjective-morphism] of etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism], each of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; the index set $I$ need not be finite. There exist a reduced Noetherian scheme $F$, a finite surjective morphism $a:F\to S$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], with $F$ an object of $\operatorname{alt}/S$ as defined in [def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology], a finite Zariski open cover $F=\bigcup_{j\in J}V_j$ [def-weil-open-immersion], indices $i(j)\in I$, and $S$-morphisms $V_j\to U_{i(j)}$. Equivalently, the maps $V_j\to S$ factor through the indicated $U_{i(j)}$. When $S$ is empty one may take $F$ and the open covering empty. No normality, regularity or degree restriction is imposed.

source.place: Expose II Proposition 3.1.1, ordinary case (parameter 1), and 3.1.2, printed p.28; finite extraction by quasi-compactness of the finite source. This is only the etale-generator case, not an arbitrary alteration cover.

proof.text: If $S=\varnothing$, take $F=\varnothing$ and $J=\varnothing$. Otherwise, $S$ is locally Noetherian by its given affine cover, and is quasi-compact because that cover is finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], it is quasi-separated. Form $U=\coprod_{i\in I}U_i$ and its induced map $u:U\to S$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. On the open summand $U_i$ the map $u$ is exactly $u_i$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source] makes $u$ etale. Every point of $S$ has a lift in a summand by joint surjectivity, so $u$ is surjective. No finiteness of $I$ or of $U$ is needed here.

source.place: Tag 09Z0, label lemma-there-is-a-scheme-integral-over; passage from a covering family to its coproduct. Quasi-separatedness: Properties Tag 01OY, label lemma-locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated.

proof.text: Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-refinement-etale-cover] to the surjective etale map $u$ and the qcqs target $S$. Obtain a finite, finitely presented, surjective map $r:Y\to S$, a finite open cover $Y=\bigcup_{a\in A}W_a$, and maps $\phi_a:W_a\to U$ with $u\circ\phi_a=r|_{W_a}$. This application does not impose any extra hypothesis on the given $u_i$.

source.place: Tag 09Z0, label lemma-there-is-a-scheme-integral-over, statement; this gives the ordinary-case refinement of ILO II Proposition 3.1.1.

proof.text: A finite map is of finite type: on an affine target its finitely many module generators also generate its algebra [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Consequently $Y$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components] and [lem-sc-scheme-sober], $S$ has finitely many irreducible components $S_1,\dots,S_m$, with generic points $\eta_1,\dots,\eta_m$, and $S=S_1\cup\dots\cup S_m$ by [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres](2) the set $A=r^{-1}(\{\eta_1,\dots,\eta_m\})$ is finite. Put $Z=\overline A=\bigcup_{y\in A}\overline{\{y\}}$ and let $j:F=Z_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow Y$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]: $F$ is reduced and $j$ maps $F$ homeomorphically onto $Z$ (this is $Y_{\mathrm{md}}$ of ILO II 1.2.5). Each $\overline{\{y\}}$ is closed and irreducible. An irreducible component $C$ of $Z$ lies in this finite union, hence in some $\overline{\{y\}}$, so $C=\overline{\{y\}}$ by maximality and its unique generic point [lem-sc-scheme-sober] is $y\in A$. Thus every generic point of $F$ maps to some $\eta_k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres](1) $r(Z)$ is closed; it contains every $\eta_k$ because $r$ is surjective, hence every $S_k=\overline{\{\eta_k\}}$, hence $S$. So $a=r\circ j:F\to S$ is surjective. It is finite directly on affine charts: if $r^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}R)=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ a finite $R$-module, the closed immersion $j$ identifies the inverse image in $F$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; the images of the module generators generate $B/J$ over $R$. Thus $a$ is finite, and $F$ is Noetherian by the same finite-type result.

source.place: Expose II 1.2.5 (X_md = closure of the image of the generic fibre with its reduced structure) and 1.2.8, printed pp.25--26; finite-map affine quotient calculation. Stacks Tag 01T6, label lemma-finite-type-noetherian, and Tag 01WN, label lemma-finite-proper.

proof.text: For a generic point $x$ of $F$, put $s=a(x)$, a generic point of $S$ by step 3. The base change $F_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-field-affine-finite-dim], write $F_s=\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $C$ finite-dimensional over $\kappa(s)$. The fibre-point identification [def-pc-scheme-fibre] gives a point $z\in F_s$ above $x$. Its residue field is $\kappa(x)$: apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field] to $\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(s)=\kappa(x)$, whose unique prime is zero. The point $z$ corresponds to a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $C$; the domain $C/\mathfrak q$ is still finite-dimensional, hence is a field by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field]. Therefore it equals its fraction field $\kappa(x)$, giving $[\kappa(x):\kappa(s)]<\infty$. Together with reducedness and finite type from step 3, these are exactly the object conditions in [def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology]. Thus $F$ belongs to $\operatorname{alt}/S$.

source.place: Expose II Definition 1.2.2 and 1.2.5--1.2.6, printed pp.24--25; finite generic fibres give finite residue extensions. Stacks finite-map base change and finite-dimensional algebra calculation.

proof.text: Pull back $W_a$ along $j$ to the open $O_a=j^{-1}(W_a)\subset F$ and compose its map to $W_a$ with $\phi_a$, obtaining $\psi_a:O_a\to U$. For every $i\in I$ put $V_{a,i}=\psi_a^{-1}(U_i)$, using the open summands of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. These are open subschemes of $F$ and cover it: choose $a$ containing a point, and then the unique summand containing its image in $U$. Restricting $\psi_a$ and identifying the corresponding summand with $U_i$ gives $V_{a,i}\to U_i$; its composite to $S$ is $a|_{V_{a,i}}$ by the equality of step 2. As $F$ is Noetherian, it is quasi-compact, so this open cover has a finite subcover. Index the selected pairs $(a,i)$ by a finite set $J$ and set $i(j)=i$. These opens and maps give every asserted factorization; empty selected opens can be omitted.

source.place: Expose II Proposition 3.1.1 (ordinary case) and 3.1.2, printed p.28; finite extraction is the definition of quasi-compactness. Coproduct summand restriction makes the family indices explicit.
